title: Deep wine farshi gharara for a nikah
concept_summary: A composed nikah concept built on a farshi gharara in the bride's own deep wine, fitted through the knee before its flare lengthens into a floor-sweeping fall. Antique gold dabka works across a band-collared kurti, and an ivory dupatta is drawn across the front while a hijab keeps the hair covered throughout.

garment_breakdown.overall_form: A long band-collared kurti over farshi gharara trousers fitted to the knee before a floor-pooling flare.
garment_breakdown.silhouette: A close upper leg giving way to a wide below-knee flare that lengthens along the floor.
garment_breakdown.drape_or_layering: The dupatta is carried across the front while a separate hijab covers the hair.
garment_breakdown.key_proportions: A long, covering kurti balanced against the weight of the pooling gharara flare.

colour_story.palette_summary: A deep wine ground warmed by antique gold, with ivory lifting the drape.
colour_story.placement: Deep wine carries the kurti and gharara, antique gold works the borders, and ivory lightens the dupatta.
colour_story.rationale: The wine reads formal for a nikah while gold and ivory keep the whole from turning heavy.

fabrics_and_texture.finish_and_movement: A textured, slightly slubbed weave that holds the gharara's structured flare.
A fine, lightly metallic sheer that keeps the drape airy over a covered head.

embellishment_plan.density: Worked richly through the borders, cuffs and collar rather than scattered across the ground.
embellishment_plan.restraint_notes: Plain wine ground is left between the worked borders so the metalwork stays legible.

coverage_and_drape.sleeves: Full-length fitted sleeves reaching the wrists.
coverage_and_drape.neckline: An upright band collar standing at the neck.
coverage_and_drape.back_and_midriff: A covered back and a fully covered waist with no bare skin.
coverage_and_drape.head_covering: A hijab covers the hair and neck throughout.
coverage_and_drape.dupatta_or_saree_drape: The ivory dupatta is carried across the front of the body.

cultural_context.regional_direction: A broad Pakistani bridal influence guides the gharara construction and the border-led metalwork.
interpretation_notes: Treated as one broad regional direction, never a fixed rule for any family or community.
safeguards: The gharara is kept distinct from a sharara, with its flare beginning below the knee.

styling_notes: Warm-toned jewellery echoes the antique gold work.
Keep the hijab styling simple so the collar stays visible.
construction_caveats: This is a concept visualisation, not a sewing pattern, and includes no measurements.
It does not guarantee that the garment can be constructed exactly as shown.
image_alt_text: A model in a deep wine farshi gharara with antique gold borderwork, a band collar, full sleeves, an ivory front-draped dupatta and a hijab.
